description: A deputy general counsel for technology transactions must finalize an outbound patent license to Meridian Systems, including its field-of-use, component, sublicensing, and improvement-rights terms, with input from patent counsel, R&D counsel, and the commercial relationship lead.

shared_context.S1: Meridian Systems wants to sign an outbound license for the company's patent portfolio next week.
shared_context.S2: The proposed transaction concerns analytics software used by industrial customers.
shared_context.S3: The current draft grants Meridian an exclusive license, permits sublicensing, and gives Meridian rights in improvements developed during the license term.
shared_context.S4: Under the team's standard transaction process, Elena conducts a final legal checkpoint in which patent, R&D, and commercial representatives each give one report in turn; after all three reports, Elena records the binding license decision in that meeting without waiting for an outside confirmation.

PF1.text: While reviewing the company's 2018 university license and related amendments, Tom confirmed that the company may grant exclusivity only for industrial analytics; healthcare and other fields must remain available to the company. He found the restriction in the executed amendment but has not circulated it in the current license-markup thread.

PF2.text: Nia checked the current prototype and confirmed that component U-7 is owned by a university and is not covered by the company's sublicense rights. The outbound license must exclude U-7 and require written university consent before any licensed deployment containing it; her lab-record confirmation is awaiting inclusion in the transaction checklist.

PF3.text: During a client-priority call this week, Meridian's general counsel said Meridian will proceed only if it may sublicense the licensed analytics to its named distributor, Orion Industrial, while the company retains ownership and use of all background technology and newly developed improvements. Marcus recorded the instruction in his relationship notes but it is not in the draft term sheet.

acceptance_conditions: Exclusivity must be limited to industrial analytics, with healthcare and other fields retained by the company.
Component U-7 must be excluded from the license.
The agreement must permit sublicensing to Orion Industrial.
The agreement must require written university consent before any licensed deployment containing U-7.
The company must retain ownership and use of all background technology and newly developed improvements.

content_checks.C2: 'industrial analytics' in decisions['exclusivity_scope'] and 'healthcare' in decisions['exclusivity_scope'] and 'company' in decisions['exclusivity_scope']
content_checks.C5: decisions['u7_excluded'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'string' and 'written university consent' in c['detail'] and 'U-7' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['named_distributor_sublicense'] == True and 'retains ownership' in decisions['improvement_rights'] and 'background technology' in decisions['improvement_rights'] and 'improvements' in decisions['improvement_rights']

decisive_facts.why: The executed 2018 amendment changes the exclusivity scope to industrial analytics and requires healthcare and other fields to remain available to the company.
The confirmed university ownership of U-7 changes the license by requiring U-7's exclusion and written university consent before any deployment containing it.

Meridian's stated transaction condition changes the sublicensing provision to name Orion Industrial and changes the improvement-rights provision to preserve the company's ownership and use of background technology and newly developed improvements.
